title: Diagnosis, treatment and prevention of ankle sprains: update of an evidence-based clinical guideline
claims: The Ottawa Ankle Rules indicate an X-ray when there is pain on the dorsal side of one or both malleoli, palpation pain at the base of the fifth metatarsal, palpation pain of the navicular bone, or inability to walk at least four steps; sensitivity is 86%-99% and negative predictive value 97%-99%.
Severity of ligament damage can be assessed most reliably by delayed physical examination 4-5 days after trauma.

The guideline states RICE is not advised as a treatment modality after a lateral ankle sprain, immobilisation should not be used, and functional support (preferably a brace) for 4-6 weeks is preferred over immobilisation.
Exercise therapy should be started as soon as possible to recover joint function; early exercise reduces recurrent sprains (RR 0.62, 95% CI 0.51-0.76) and functional ankle instability.
Brace or tape reduces recurrent sprains (RR 0.30, 95% CI 0.21-0.43) and first-time sprains (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.49-0.96).
NSAIDs may be used to reduce pain and swelling, but care is advised because they may suppress the natural healing process.

Return timeline: a distortion can return to full work and sports at 3-4 weeks; a partial or total ligament rupture mostly returns at 6-8 weeks depending on physiotherapy results; patients after surgery return to physically demanding sports at 12-16 weeks.
Surgery is reserved for patients who need a quick recovery, such as professional athletes, or whose complaints are not resolved by thorough conservative exercise-based treatment.
